title: SLEEPP - Stress-lowering EffEcts of Parental Presence
summary: This study aims to investigate the effect of a parent’s or other close caregiver’s presence during the induction of anesthesia on children’s stress levels. To this end, children—both those accompanied by a caregiver and those who are not—will be studied, and saliva samples will be collected at various time points to measure stress markers. In addition, the stress levels of the parents and the anesthesia team, as well as the depth of anesthesia, will be recorded. After anesthesia, any pain and temporary states of confusion (delirium) experienced by the children in the recovery room will be assessed. The results from the two groups will be compared to identify any differences resulting from the presence of a caregiver.

interventions.name: This prospective clinical study is designed as a feasibility study with an adaptive design in the form of a “before-and-after comparison.
